title: Injective acyclicity gives sheaf-level base change for arbitrary coefficients
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring and let $f:X\to Y$ be a proper morphism of schemes [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Assume coefficient-wise injective acyclicity: for every prime $\ell$, every morphism $g:Y'\to Y$, every cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] with induced $f':X'\to Y'$ and $g':X'\to X$, and every injective sheaf $I$ of $(\Lambda/\ell)_X$-modules on $X_{\Et}$, one has $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I=0$ for all $q>0 (higher direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] of the inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] of the underlying abelian sheaf). Then for every such square and every sheaf $F$ of $\Lambda_X$-modules with torsion underlying abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$, regarded as a complex concentrated in degree 0, the derived exchange morphism $\Ex_{\square,F}:g^{-1}Rf_*F\to Rf'_*g'^{-1}F$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] is an isomorphism in $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories].

source.place: Lemma 0A4B (lemma-proper-base-change-in-terms-of-injectives), proof paragraphs 2-3: prime-torsion dévissage, induction on the annihilator, and filtered-colimit passage

proof.text: For the torsion underlying sheaf write $F=\varinjlim_nF[n]$ [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-torsion-devissage]. Properness makes $f$ and every base change $f'$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so higher direct images along $f$ and $f'$ commute with this filtered colimit by [lemma-weil-pbc-direct-image-filtered-colimit] (the $F[n]$ and $g'^{-1}F[n]$ are torsion), while $g^{-1}$ and $g'^{-1}$ commute with colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-preserves-colimits]. Since $g^{-1}$ is exact, $\mathcal H^q(\Ex_{\square,F})$ is the base change map $g^{-1}R^qf_*F\to R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F$, and by the naturality of $\Ex_\square$ in its argument [lemma-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-replacement] applied to the inclusions $F[n]\to F$ it is, under these colimit isomorphisms, the filtered colimit of the maps $\mathcal H^q(\Ex_{\square,F[n]})$. A filtered colimit of isomorphisms is an isomorphism, and a morphism of $\Dplus(Y'_{\Et})$ inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-derived-plus-iso-on-cohomology]; so it suffices to treat the sheaves $F[n]$, each a $\Lambda_X$-module killed by $n$.

For each $n$, the prime-torsion dévissage [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-torsion-devissage] supplies the short exact sequences $0\to G[\ell]\to G\xrightarrow{\ell}\ell G\to0$ of torsion $\Lambda_X$-modules, with $\ell G$ killed by $n/\ell$ when $nG=0$. For such a sequence the exchange maps form a morphism between the long exact sequences of higher direct images, and exchange is an isomorphism in every degree for $G$ once it is for $G[\ell]$ and $\ell G$ [lemma-weil-pbc-five-lemma-transfer] (the five lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] on the morphism of triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-triangulated]). By induction on the number of prime factors of $n$ [lemma-weil-pbc-prime-factor-induction] it suffices to treat a sheaf killed by one prime $\ell$.

source.place: Lemma 0A4B, proof paragraph 2 (induction and five lemma)

proof.text: Let $\ell F=0$ and regard $F$ as a sheaf of $(\Lambda/\ell)$-modules. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-enough-injectives] choose an injective resolution $F\to I^\bullet$ in $\Mod(X_{\Et},\Lambda/\ell)$, $I^m=0$ for $m<0$. Each $I^m$ is killed by $\ell$, hence torsion, and by the coefficient-wise IA hypothesis $R^qf'_*g'^{-1}I^m=0$ for $q>0$; for the identity square ($g=\mathrm{id}_Y$) also $R^qf_*I^m=0$ for $q>0$. All of this is about underlying abelian sheaves. Let $J=I(F)$ be the K-injective complex of abelian sheaves chosen for $F$ in the definition of $Rf_*$ [def-weil-pbc-direct-image] [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], with $s=\rho_F$; by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] the isomorphism $QI^\bullet\cong QF\cong QJ$ is $Q(h)$ for a quasi-isomorphism of complexes $h:I^\bullet\to J$ under $F$, and likewise the chosen resolution of $g'^{-1}J$ is $Q(j)$ for a quasi-isomorphism $j:g'^{-1}J\to J'$ with $J'$ K-injective. By [lem-weil-pbc-derived-exchange-termwise], applied with $(J,s)$ and $j$, $\Ex_{\square,F}$ is $Q(e_J)$ with $e_J=f'_*(j)\circ\Ex^0_{\square,J}$, up to the isomorphisms $\sigma_{\rm src},\sigma_{\rm tgt}$. Termwise naturality of $\Ex^0_\square$ [lemma-weil-pbc-underived-exchange-naturality] for $h$ gives $e_J\circ g^{-1}f_*(h)=f'_*(g'^{-1}I\to g'^{-1}J\to J')\circ\Ex^0_{\square,I}$. Here $g^{-1}f_*(h)$ is a quasi-isomorphism, because $f_*(h)$ is one by the Leray criterion for complexes [lemma-weil-pbc-leray-acyclicity](3) applied to the $f_*$-acyclic $I^m$, and $g^{-1}$ is exact; likewise $f'_*$ of the quasi-isomorphism $g'^{-1}I\to J'$ is a quasi-isomorphism by the same criterion applied to the $f'_*$-acyclic $g'^{-1}I^m$; and $\Ex^0_{\square,I}$ is an isomorphism of complexes, termwise by [lemma-weil-pbc-proper-underived-exchange] since $f$ is proper and the $I^m$ are torsion. Hence $Q(e_J)$, and so $\Ex_{\square,F}$, is an isomorphism.
